heroHeadline: US Q1 GDP +2.0% Beats Forecast — But March PCE Surges to 3.5% Headline; ECB Holds at 2.00%; S&P 500 Hits New ATH 7,264 as Stagflation Trap Confirmed
heroSubtitle: Apr 30–May 1: Q1 2026 GDP advance estimate beat expectations at +2.0% annualized (GDPNow had forecast 1.2%), signaling the US avoided contraction despite the Iran war energy shock — driven by AI infrastructure investment and rebounding federal spending. But simultaneously, March 2026 PCE re-accelerated to 3.5% headline / 3.2% core YoY — the hottest PCE since the Iran war began — confirming the stagflation trap that prevents any Fed pivot. The ECB held at 2.00% on April 30 as Eurozone April CPI flash hit 3.0% (from 2.3%), driven by Iran war energy costs. Tech mega-cap Q1 2026 earnings (April 29 after close) all beat: Microsoft $82.9B revenue (+18%), Alphabet $109.9B (+22%), Meta net income $26.8B (+61%), Amazon beat all estimates — combined AI capex guidance ~$500B/year. S&P 500 rose 1.02% to new ATH 7,209 (April 30) and extended to 7,264 (+0.77%) on May 1. ISM Manufacturing PMI April 2026: 52.7% (fourth consecutive expansion month). Kevin Warsh's Senate floor vote is now expected the week of May 11 — he would chair the June FOMC meeting (June 9-10) if confirmed before Powell's May 15 term expiry. Recession probabilities: Goldman Sachs ~25%, JPMorgan ~30%, Moody's Analytics ~42% (all modestly lower on GDP beat, but stagflation confirmed by PCE).
